text:
alex.k: :rotating_light: seeing container restarts in prod-gpu-pool-3 around 10:07 UTC. Multiple OOMs during prefill for long-context requests. Impacting streaming endpoints for acme-app.

alex.k: sample log: 
```
[2024-05-03T10:07:21Z] runtime ERROR: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
  at prefill_worker.cpp:142 allocate_kv_cache
  container: rtx-serve-72 restarted (exit code 137)
```

alex.k: root cause seems to be extremely long user prompts (>> 8k tokens) + concurrent prefill spikes. Prefill allocation spikes beyond device memory and containers restart.

incident-bot: :rotating_light: Page sent to on-call: @nathan.l (policy: severity=high)

nathan.l: oncall here — pulling node logs and container cores. Any confirmed customer impact?

emily.s: acme-app support report: ~12% requests returning 502/503 in last 10m. Crash IDs: rtx-serve-72 / rtx-serve-73. Graphs show memory pressure correlating with long prompt traces.

nathan.l: ok isolating traffic away from gpu-pool-3 now. Will update routing to avoid the pool while we triage.

juan.r: hot mitigation idea: apply a temporary prefill-trim policy per-tenant (max_prefill_tokens=2048) for acme-app to avoid huge allocations. Low risk and fast rollback.

priya.m: also propose enabling the smallseq-fallback model variant for requests where token_count > 4k — that'll route to a model with smaller KV footprint.

nathan.l: applying routing change now. Command: 
```
curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/v1/routes/apply \
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
 -d '{"selector":"acme-app/*","policy":"prefill_trim","max_tokens":2048}'
```

sre-bot: routing change accepted. 60% of acme-app traffic diverted to cpu-fallback, 40% to smallseq-fallback.

emily.s: customer errors dropping — 502s down to ~2% within 3 minutes after routing change. Monitoring continuing.

alex.k: logs also show occasional "CUDA error: device-side assert" after repeated OOMs; might indicate kernel instability after multiple failed allocs. Recommend replacing nodes in that pool.

nathan.l: starting node replace for nodes in gpu-pool-3 (drain -> remove -> reprovision). Job id: nr-881.

juan.r: additional temporary throttle: set prefill-concurrency=1 for heavy-context routes, to avoid concurrent spikes.

priya.m: working on a runtime hotpatch to fallback to CPU coldmodel when prefill allocation fails instead of letting the container crash. PR#1256. Will canary it after routing changes.

nathan.l: hotpatch applied to canary cluster, observing stable behavior across a couple of cycles — no new restarts.

incident-bot: PagerDuty incident created: INC-20240503-229 (sev: high) — handoff scheduled to morning oncall at 11:00 UTC.

emily.s: drafting customer-facing message for Support: 
"Hi Acme team — we observed intermittent failures on your streaming endpoint caused by very large prefill allocations for long prompts. We've rerouted traffic and applied temporary trimming rules. We're replacing impacted nodes and deploying a hotpatch to reduce crash risk. We'll follow up with a timeline and proposed safeguards."

alex.k: please send that update. Also: collect example long requests (anonymized) that triggered the failure for postmortem.

emily.s: posting update to #support and pinging acme-app now. :thumbsup:

nathan.l: next steps (live): 1) complete node replacements (nr-881) 2) promote hotpatch cluster-wide 3) add long-prompt rate limit & alert 4) assign postmortem owner: juan.r

juan.r: taking postmortem. I'll start draft and add timeline + metric graphs.

alex.k: follow-ups for platform: add per-request prefill KV memory accounting, router-side token estimation, and automatic prefill-trim for >8k tokens. Also instrument `prefill_alloc_attempts` metric and emit event on first CUDA OOM.

priya.m: adding a monitor to fire when prefill_alloc_attempts > 3 within 5m for any node.

sre-bot: node-replace nr-881 succeeded, new nodes healthy, containers stabilized.

nathan.l: marking incident as mitigated for live traffic. Keeping thread open for postmortem notes and customer follow-ups.

emily.s: customer updated, they acknowledged and requested ETA for hotpatch promotion. I gave tentative ETA 2 hours.

alex.k: thanks all. Sync for postmortem tomorrow 15:00 UTC.

nathan.l: leaving follow-up todo: (1) ensure routing rule rollback plan (2) run a large-context load test against staging with hotpatch (3) add docs for oncall runbook for long-prefill OOMs.

emily.s: closing slack updates, will update incident ticket with links. :eyes:
